idiom_name: test-specific replacement object whose indirect answers are programmed before the SUT is exercised
implementation_notes: Language-neutral form: declare the collaborator, or the slice of it the SUT uses, as an abstraction, then give each test a replacement that implements that abstraction and returns canned values - no interaction expectations anywhere. Programme the answers during fixture setup, before the SUT is exercised; during exercise the stub simply answers, and the test asserts the SUT's own result. Keep the answers to the cases the branch consumes (a value, an exception, a sequence), create the double per test so no programmed state leaks, and pair every stubbed contract with at least one test against the real collaborator or a fake, because the canned answers are an assumption nobody else checks. When several tests need the same collaborator with different answers, promote the per-test stub to a configurable test double or a fixture rather than copying the setup.
code_sketch:
stub = replacement_for(Warehouse)
stub.answer("has_inventory", args=("Talisker", 50), returns=False)   # configure first
install(order, stub)                    # substitutable seam
result = order.fill()                   # SUT receives the canned indirect input
assert result is False                  # assert the SUT, never the stub
pitfalls: Programming an answer after the SUT already holds the double, or after the call, has no effect in most frameworks - configure first, then hand it over.
An unconfigured method answers a default (null, 0, false, undefined, another mock), which can send the SUT down a path the test never intended.
The canned answers are never checked against the real collaborator unless a contract test exists; treat the stub as a hypothesis.

Constructing the SUT requires five collaborators and the test stubs all five although it asserts on none of them: those are Dummies, and the resulting Elaborate Fixture hides the one answer the branch actually consumes behind setup noise.

Canned payloads that are structurally valid but semantically impossible - a zero-row page with next_cursor set, a declined payment carrying a capture timestamp - keep the test green against a state production can never emit, so the SUT branch it covers exists only in the stub.
